- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with sentiment momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overcorrects downward; reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts remain flat or rising, adjust downward by 2–4% to reflect mean reversion toward lower range.  
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; add 0.5–1.5% to early forecast to capture sentiment lag.  
- In multi-day forecast windows (e.g., 30d), model tends to overestimate later periods when sentiment is bullish; apply a 1–3% downward bias to final 5–7 days to reflect sentiment decay.
